caption: The drawing features three distinct brass or brass-colored keyhole escutcheons, each with a different design, arranged vertically within a rectangular frame. Each escutcheon includes a central keyhole, decorative plates, and an attached handle or knocker. The top escutcheon is elaborately shaped, with symmetrical, flowing curves on either side and a circular design on the right. It has a small, round handle attached to the left side. The middle and bottom escutcheons share a similar overall form; both have a more angular outline with straight and curved elements, a prominent central keyhole surrounded by a raised edge, diamond-shaped cutouts to the left and right of the keyhole, and a handle attached to the left side with a circular mechanical component securing it. The handles on these two escutcheons are comma-shaped and metallic, colored with shades of green and gold to depict the brass material and shadows. Just below the lowest escutcheon, there is a horizontal ruler marked "O" to "2 inch" for scale. The artist's name, "HANS KORSCH," is written in the lower left corner. The drawing uses black outlines and careful shading to illustrate the forms, and the background is an uncolored, off-white paper.
title: Three Door Handles
